verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — X wins on one hard, verified, key-item difference. Y rejects bin/cc-do:454 with the assertion "None of the non-comment `deploy-live` lines in scope passes it as a `--run` argument", which scripts/deploy-live.sh:812 refutes directly (`"$BACKLOG_BIN" needs "$title" --run "$run"`, with $run built at :708/:728/:731/:734/:743/:746 and read back by cc-do at :415 before the exec at :454). That false premise makes Y's answer to brief part (a) 6 where 7 is right, and it also corrupts Y's own near-miss entry for deploy-live.sh:708-746 ("escalation/page record" only). X counts that site and traces the producer correctly. Y is genuinely better on method — 316-hit denominator, four grep-verified negatives, three verified stale-citation catches, the most complete near-miss sweep (I confirmed all ten "remaining files are comments" myself), and it reads cc-do's dispatch (:525/:535-540/:543-548) that X explicitly left unread and substituted a usage comment for — but a positively asserted falsehood that changes the headline count outweighs a richer periphery.

X vs Z — Z wins, narrowly. Both reach 16 key items and the same correct total of 7, and both trace the cc-premise and cc-do:454 dispatchers to their producers. The separation is in what each verified: Z produced four stale-citation findings (ship-land.sh:1703's deploy-live.sh:2543, the plist:16 → operator-readout:238-246 cite, cc-do:152's §152-258, and — uniquely — deploy-live.sh:185 calling deploy-now "`deploy-live.sh --force`" when deploy-now.sh:89 forwards only `"$@"`), where X produced none and instead leaned on two comments, including deploy-now.sh:69-70 as its in-scope corroboration for question (c), which is precisely the grounding the brief forbade. Z also read cc-do's dispatch reach and the non-tty exit-3 path that X declined to read, and it alone states the count's sensitivity to the brief's "stored advisory string" exclusion. The cost is real: Z carries three off-by-one citations (cc-do:358 for :359's code, cc-do:357 for the :358 CONFIRM branch, operator-readout:533 for the :532 test) and a wrong self-reported grep count of 273 against the actual 316, where X's ~35 checked citations were all clean. None of Z's slips changes a conclusion; X's omissions leave a required deliverable unattempted.

Y vs Z — Z wins on the same decisive point that separated X from Y, and with fewer offsetting gaps than X had. Z counts bin/cc-do:454 and traces the exact path Y declared nonexistent (deploy-live.sh:708-746 → :812 `needs --run` → cc-do:415 → :454), giving the correct total of 7 against Y's 6. Elsewhere the two are close: both correctly reject bin/cc-backlog:4308 on the same verified ground, both catch the `-` vs `:-` seam at deploy-now.sh:56, both read the dispatch reach and the non-tty exit 3, both hedge N4 the same way and both miss the autonomy-sweep scheduled path. Y is cleaner on citations (zero bad against Z's three off-by-one) and has the broader verified near-miss sweep; Z has the unique deploy-live.sh:185 catch and the explicit count-sensitivity note. Those trade roughly evenly, leaving Y's verified false premise and wrong total as the deciding difference.
